notes: Accept, with two kinds of correction in place. The recorded hash reproduces (a07fcb79…) — the extraction records only the DOI, and the Centre Mersenne PDF at that DOI gives exactly that hash — and I re-extracted all 159 pages, printed 69–227. Structure: 273 items (255 missing, 11 planned, 7 library), every missing item routed exactly once, all planned layer ids exist, all fifteen routes' stages exist, all six Part II parents exist, all areas are galaxy ids, and check_paper.py passes. One stage, AnalyticStacks:AS.1, is not in data/atlas.json: it is in the designed roadmap research/blueprint/roadmaps/AnalyticStacks.json, which three other extractions also route to, so it is fine. All twelve declarations behind the seven library items resolve at the pins, from RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular and localCohomology to Tau Ceti's cohomologyModule family, Subadditive.tendsto_lim and AddCircle.denseRange_zsmul_coe_iff. First correction: the locators. The item locators name the paper's numbered results, and in 67 of them the kind word is wrong — Lemma for Proposition, Theorem for Corollary, Lemma for Definition and so on (50 distinct results: 2.48, 2.51–2.53, 4.17–4.20, 4.23–4.27, 4.29, 6.9–6.14, 6.18, 6.25, 6.27, 6.28, 7.13, 7.18, 8.2, 8.6, 8.10, 8.11, 8.14, 8.20, 8.22, 8.23, 8.25, 8.27, 9.6–9.9, 9.13, 9.19–9.21, 9.24, 9.30, 9.33, 9.36, 10.2, 10.4, 10.5 and others). The numbers are right; I checked a sample at the pages and corrected the kind words to what the paper prints, leaving external citations ('Pat18 Theorem 9.7', 'Bha20 Theorem 3.4', 'SGA7 XVII') and the arXiv-version numbering in E1's locator untouched. Second correction: the PrismaticCohomology Part II title, whose prefix read 'Prismatic cohomology' where the parent's atlas title is 'Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants'; the other five Part II titles already reproduced their parents exactly. All eight findings are confirmed at their locators in the published text. Two are the paper contradicting itself: Theorem 9.28(c) prints a strict bound where the introduction's Theorem I(c) and the proof's Lemma 9.29 are non-strict (E4), and Theorem 10.6 prints β(1) = 393 where Theorem K prints 373 (E5). E6 and E7 have immediate counterexamples — g^{−1}(X) is not a divisor, and the minimum over an empty linear system does not exist — and E1, E2, E3 and E8 are as recorded, each read at its page. Nothing was rejected or deleted and I add no finding: I read the published text at each finding, the statements the routes cite and a sample of the corrected locators, not all 159 pages line by line.
